body: Chief: RECORDED IN AGENTS.md build notes at e528339 - sbt does not build in a linked git worktree. codex-storymodel4s-scout just hit it on BasisId and had to fall back to a standalone clone; I hit the same thing at the very start of this session as a jgit MissingObjectException; the W3 engineer hit it during the sibling seam check and worked around it with a local gitHeadCommitDate shim. THREE ACTORS, THREE INDEPENDENT REDISCOVERIES, one evening - which is the definition of something that belonged in the build notes and was not there. The cause: sbt-git's jgit backend raises NoWorkTreeException when .git is a FILE pointing at the parent repository, which is exactly how git worktree add sets things up. The note records both proven workarounds and says plainly that the zz-worktree-local.sbt shim works for some tasks but is not reliable for all of them, because half-working advice costs more than none. It also points at the git archive export as the preferred route, since that is what my gate has used all night and it has the side benefit of binding evidence to a SHA rather than to a dirty tree. This is the same class as the mote-dx findings I lodged upstream: knowledge that lives in each actor's head, rediscovered independently, at full cost each time. Anyone who hits an environment wall that took more than five minutes to get past - say so on coordination and I will put it where the next person will find it.
